newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Peregrine Chairman Philip Tose told Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in Hong Kong on Monday that his company was working on setting up a Bangladesh Fund to invest in the country's stock markets. Tose said he was expecting assistance from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank for the fund.

Bangladesh is reviewing performances of private universities now operating on temporary government permission. The review report by the University Grants Commission, expected in a month, will decide the fate of the universities.

Poor maintenance of railway tracks was a major cause of Saturday's train accident near Dhaka which killed at least seven people, according to mechanical experts in Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology.

A special cabinet committee on law and order has directed police to take harsh measures to curb terrorism and extortion of money. Home (interior) Minister Rafiqul Islam asked law enforcing agencies to arrest terrorists irrespective of party affiliation.
Bangladesh has requested the Asian Trade Promotion Forum to take steps for equitable development of its member countries in the Asia Pacific region.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Moudud Ahmed, who lost in September 5 parliamentary by-elections, complained to foreign diplomats that the Election Commission had failed to act neutrally.

The United Arab Emirates' national airline Emirates will start operating regular flights between Dhaka and the Malaysian capital Kuala Lampur by end of the current month. The airline will operate three flight a week. -- Dhaka Newsroom 880-2-506363
